Sweep a range of cluster numbers

Source: R/clustering.R
sweepClusterK.Rd

Scores a partition at each k over a range, so the number of clusters is chosen from the data rather than fixed by hand. Returns the scores and a plot marking the k the chosen criterion favors.

Usage

sweepClusterK(
  gobject = NULL,
  spat_unit = NULL,
  feat_type = NULL,
  values_to_use = c("dim_reduction", "spatial_enrichment"),
  dim_reduction_to_use = "pca",
  dim_reduction_name = NULL,
  dimensions_to_use = 1:10,
  spat_enr_name = NULL,
  x = NULL,
  k_range = 2:15,
  cluster_method = c("kmeans", "hclust"),
  score = c("silhouette", "wss", "gap"),
  dist_method = c("euclidean", "correlation"),
  hclust_method = "ward.D2",
  subsample = NULL,
  max_dist_obs = 20000L,
  seed = NULL,
  nstart = 5,
  iter_max = 50,
  n_perm = 25,
  line_color = "grey60",
  point_color = "#C44E52",
  title = NULL,
  xlab = NULL,
  ylab = NULL,
  axis_text = 9,
  axis_title = 10,
  theme_param = list(),
  output = c("plot", "data.table"),
  verbose = NULL,
  view = NULL,
  show_plot = NULL,
  return_plot = NULL,
  save_plot = NULL,
  save_param = list(),
  default_save_name = "sweepClusterK"
)

Arguments

gobject

giotto object. The matrix to cluster is read from one of its slots, chosen with `values_to_use`. May be NULL when `x` is given.

spat_unit

spatial unit (e.g. "cell")

feat_type

feature type (e.g. "rna", "dna", "protein")

values_to_use

character. Which slot supplies the matrix: "dim_reduction" (cluster cells in PC space), "spatial_enrichment" (cluster cells by neighborhood composition, which is how a niche k is chosen).

dim_reduction_to_use, dim_reduction_name, dimensions_to_use

Which reduction and which of its components, for `values_to_use = "dim_reduction"`. A linear reduction: "pca", "nmf", "harmony" or "lsi".

spat_enr_name

character. Enrichment to read, for `values_to_use = "spatial_enrichment"`. Defaults to the first stored.

x

numeric matrix or data.frame of observations by variables, a dist, or the list from spatialCoexpression(return_gobject = FALSE). Supplied, it is used instead of any slot. A co-expression result is not stored on a giotto object, so this is the only way to sweep co-expression modules.

k_range

integer vector of cluster numbers to score.

cluster_method

character. "kmeans" or "hclust". Forced to "hclust" for a co-expression result or a `dist`.

score

character, one or more of "silhouette", "wss" and "gap". Several are drawn as panels, which is the honest way to show that they disagree. "wss" and "gap" need coordinates, so a co-expression result or a `dist` leaves only "silhouette". Left unset, all three are scored for k-means and only "silhouette" for a hierarchical cut.

dist_method

character. Distance for the silhouette when `x` is a matrix: "euclidean" or "correlation" (`1 - r` between observations).

hclust_method

character. Passed to stats::hclust. Ignored for a co-expression result, whose own tree is used.

subsample

integer or NULL. Observations to randomly sample before scoring. A silhouette needs every pairwise distance, so it is quadratic in observations and this is the only way to run one on a large object.

max_dist_obs

integer. Refuse to build a distance above this many observations. The default of 20,000 is about 1.6 GB; half a million cells would be 892 GB, so the refusal is there to name the number rather than let the allocation fail.

seed

numeric or NULL. Seed for sampling and k-means starts.

nstart, iter_max

numeric. Passed to stats::kmeans.

n_perm

numeric. Reference datasets for the gap statistic, passed to cluster::clusGap as `B`. Ignored by the other criteria.

line_color, point_color

character. Curve and marked point.

title

character. Plot title.

xlab, ylab

character. Axis titles. NULL names the criterion on y, and on x the number swept: modules for a co-expression result, clusters otherwise.

axis_text, axis_title

numeric. Base sizes.

theme_param

list. Passed to ggplot2::theme.

output

character. "plot" (default) draws the scores; "data.table" returns them instead: one row per k per criterion, with `k`, `value`, `se` (the gap's standard error, NA for the others), `score` and `selected`.

verbose

be verbose

view

character. Name of a GiottoClass::giottoView slotted on `gobject`, resolved once before the matrix is read.

show_plot

logical. show plot

return_plot

logical. return ggplot object

save_plot

logical. save the plot

save_param

list of saving parameters, see showSaveParameters

default_save_name

default save name for saving, don't change, change save_name in save_param

Value

ggplot, or a data.table when `output = "data.table"`

Details

The criterion, not the clustering engine, is what makes this general. A silhouette needs only a partition and a distance, so the same call covers k-means over a composition matrix and a hierarchical cut of a correlation matrix. Within-cluster sum of squares applies to k-means alone, where the chosen k is the point furthest from the line joining the ends of the curve.

The list returned by spatialCoexpression(return_gobject = FALSE) is accepted directly. Its own tree is cut at each k and scored on the same `1 - r` distance it was built from, so no second tree is fitted and the k reported here is the `n_modules` to pass back to spatialCoexpression(). The `n_modules` used for that first call does not matter: the tree is the same for every k.

A silhouette is quadratic in the number of observations, so `subsample` exists for the cell-level case. It does not apply to a co-expression result, where the observations are features and the tree is already built.

Only linear reductions are read from the object. UMAP and t-SNE are refused: they distort distances, so the silhouette and wss computed on them are inflated and depend on the embedding's random seed, and on data with no clusters at all they report structure that is not there. Coordinates passed as `x` are used as given.

The marked k is the criterion's preference, not a recommendation. Criteria disagree, and a k one step either side is usually defensible.

Which arguments apply depends on the input. A setting that would change what is computed, but that the chosen input does not use, is ignored with a warning when it was set explicitly: a linkage, distance or sample for a co-expression result or a distance, a slot when `x` is supplied, or the other slot's name. Other unused arguments are ignored silently.

Examples

g <- GiottoData::loadGiottoMini("visium")

# k-means on the PCA, scored by within-cluster sum of squares
sweepClusterK(g, k_range = 2:10, score = "wss", seed = 1)

# the same partitions scored by silhouette, as a table
sweepClusterK(g, k_range = 2:10, score = "silhouette", seed = 1,
    output = "data.table")

# co-expression modules: sweep the tree spatialCoexpression() built
coexp <- spatialCoexpression(g, feats = head(rownames(g), 100),
    return_gobject = FALSE)
sweepClusterK(coexp, k_range = 2:12)
